source.title: Rethinking normalization methods in federated learning
source.authors: Zhi-Xu Du; Jing-Wei Sun; Ang Li; Pin-Yu Chen; Jianyi Zhang; H. Li; Yiran Chen

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including experimental setup, results and conclusion.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests normalization choices in federated CIFAR-10 training and reports accuracy and convergence, extending normalization findings to a federated, non-IID setting. Its results do not measure training classification error as named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own CIFAR-10 federated normalization experiments and the toy batch-normalization statistics experiment. The paper does not report training classification error, so these outcomes do not directly test V1–V6 as written. Prior-work findings in Related Work were not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 4 compares accuracy over communication rounds for the same architectures with and without batch normalization, testing V6 in non-IID federated learning. V6 does not require training classification error. However, the extracted rows record endpoints rather than accuracy-gain rates.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute impaired aggregation and batch-normalization failures to external covariate shift, and report fastest or comparable convergence and best or comparable accuracy with layer normalization. These are their mechanistic interpretation and empirical conclusions; the experiments do not establish that normalization is universally indispensable.
record.recipe_differences: Federated averaging on non-IID CIFAR10 compares normalization methods and reports global model accuracy and convergence; claim versions focus on classification training error and related centralized optimization findings.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by architecture and normalization method; for ResNet-18, no normalization slightly exceeds layer normalization, while the authors say its hyperparameters must be selected carefully for stable training.

fits_no_version.finding: At 5000 rounds, batch normalization improves VGG-11 accuracy over no normalization, 51.56% versus 36.51%, but reduces ResNet-18 accuracy, 34.38% versus 60.73%, and CNN accuracy, 33.29% versus 49.96%. These endpoints do not establish learning speed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of batch normalization on final global-model accuracy in non-IID federated learning depends on architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer normalization gives the highest or comparable endpoint accuracy across architectures; the authors also report fastest or comparable convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer normalization can improve global-model convergence and accuracy in the tested non-IID federated setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The two-device MNIST experiment shows different same-channel feature statistics after local training despite common initialization and batch normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local training can produce cross-device feature-statistics discrepancies that batch normalization does not remove.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 3rd International Workshop on Distributed Machine Learning
record.problems: The experiments use one dataset and one non-IID partition configuration. Three seeds are reported for the main accuracy experiments. The toy statistics demonstration is limited to two devices and MNIST, and its figure does not provide a numerical summary in the supplied text. The reported classification metric is accuracy, not training error.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated normalization-method accuracy rows were omitted. The paper reports accuracy for additional normalization baselines in Table 2; those rows are not linked to the listed versions and are not needed to show the layer-normalization versus batch-normalization comparison. Figure 4 convergence curves are described qualitatively without numeric values, so no separate rows were added for each plotted point.

untested.parts: Training classification error, fitting corrupted labels, and model-size or stopping effects.
Teacher-student local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts.
Initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth.
Stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, and divergence.
Higher-learning-rate tolerance and Fixup. The supplied text does not provide readable pairwise batch-normalization versus no-normalization accuracy-gain rates.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly excludes V6 because the metric is test accuracy and the setting is federated. Figure 4 makes this a new-setting test, but its pairwise speed results cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text. Its omission is already declared in rows_left_out, so no missing entry is added. No directional V6 verdict is assigned from endpoint accuracy alone.

versions.untested_parts: No training classification error, random-label fitting, model-size comparison, or early-stopping result is reported.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or local-minimum result.
No plain-versus-residual depth sweep or training-error comparison.
No initialization comparison or trainable-depth experiment.
No learning-rate stability threshold, sharpness, or training-loss result.

Although normalization methods are compared in federated training, the paper reports test accuracy and convergence rather than the version's accuracy-gain rate and learning-rate tolerance in its stated centralized settings; it also does not test Fixup.

datasets are the same except having different mean values

rows.measure: Histograms of output before and after BatchNorm by channel
rows.value: The paper states that devices have totally different feature statistics for the same channel; second- and third-layer input distributions normalize to similar statistics while output channels still show significant statistical discrepancy.
rows.note: Feature statistics are measured, not training classification error.
rows.check: Cross-device feature-statistics discrepancies do not directly measure training speed, learning-rate tolerance, or another listed version.
